title: Validate a cart and spring model
purpose: Connect a force model, calculus, mechanical energy, numerical integration, uncertainty, and technical reporting. Oscillatory behavior is an application here; the full oscillations course belongs to PHS 232.
requiredRoute: Browser simulation with a downloadable time table and a saved structured notebook. Label all generated observations simulated. It is a conceptual and computational investigation, not a physical laboratory credit.
officialEquipment: No PHS 231 equipment requirement was established by the current public description. Do not infer the introductory physics lab's kit requirement for this lecture course.

model.system: One-dimensional mass m on an ideal horizontal spring with stiffness k; optional viscous resistance b.
model.domain: m>0, k>0, b>=0; small displacement in the spring's stated linear range; rigid cart, no dry friction, no end stops, and fixed reference at equilibrium.
model.anchorChecks: Initial energy 0.0256 J; angular frequency 4 rad/s; initial acceleration -1.28 m/s^2. For b=0, x(t)=0.08 cos(4t), v(t)=-0.32 sin(4t), period pi/2 s. Derive these independently before relying on the simulator.

tasks.instructions: State a measurable question about the influence of step size or damping. Define coordinates, system boundary, units, and every idealization.
tasks.evidence: A model statement and a prediction about displacement, velocity, and energy trends before running the simulation.

tasks.instructions: Derive acceleration and initial energy from the parameters. For the undamped baseline, verify the supplied cosine solution by two derivatives and initial conditions; predict its period and first equilibrium-crossing speed.
tasks.evidence: Labeled calculations and one dimensional check; crossing speed magnitude 0.32 m/s, first crossing velocity -0.32 m/s.

tasks.instructions: Run explicit and semi-implicit Euler at all three step sizes. Record the exact update order. Compare position at identical times with the analytic baseline and compute the largest absolute energy residual over each run.
tasks.evidence: Six run records with method, h, duration, initial conditions, final errors, and energy residuals. Explain step-halving trends without claiming the semi-implicit method exactly conserves energy.

tasks.instructions: Add b=0.2 kg/s while holding the other parameters fixed. Halve the smallest step again. Compare the mechanical-energy change with a numerical integral of -b v^2.
tasks.evidence: A trace/table, a dissipation ledger, and a residual. Explain why energy loss is expected and how discretization error differs from physical damping.

tasks.instructions: Treat m in [0.49,0.51] kg and k in [7.8,8.2] N/m as supplied bounded inputs. Predict the undamped period interval from its monotonic dependence on m and k. Compare interval spread with numerical step sensitivity.
tasks.evidence: Endpoint calculation with seconds, explanation of which endpoints maximize and minimize period, and a statement that bounded inputs are not probability distributions.

tasks.instructions: Explain whether the original question was answered, identify one unsupported assumption, propose a discriminating next measurement, and revise one claim after inspecting residuals.
tasks.evidence: A reproducible notebook including raw simulated data provenance, calculations, comparison, limitations, and revision. Save, reload, export a backup, and confirm restored content.

rubric.scale: 0 absent/incorrect; 1 partial with material gap; 2 adequate and reproducible; 3 correct with a justified independent check.
criteria: Analytic prediction with units and initial conditions
rubric.completionDefault: At least 2 in every criterion plus all required evidence. Numeric checks support the rubric but do not automatically grade reasoning. A self-rating is labeled self-assessment; independent review is recorded only if actually provided.

optionalPhysicalExtension.activity: Observe a small, freely moving object in an existing safe tabletop setup and compare position timing with a model, only if suitable equipment is already available.
optionalPhysicalExtension.safety: Do not build launchers, suspend overhead masses, stretch high-energy springs, break material samples, use rotating power tools, or pressurize containers. Keep motion low energy and contained, clear the area, and stop if a spring, support, or attachment is damaged. The required simulation needs none of these activities.
optionalPhysicalExtension.measurement: Record instrument resolution, camera frame interval if used, parallax, timing uncertainty, mass and length estimates, repetitions, and raw observations. Do not substitute simulation output for missing physical measurements.
optionalPhysicalExtension.evidenceDistinction: Optional physical observations can extend the report, but are not claimed to satisfy an official NU lab, instrument competency, or equipment requirement.
